newsitem.title: USA: Dixon Ticonderoga buys Mexican unit shares.
newsitem.headline: Dixon Ticonderoga buys Mexican unit shares.

text.p: Dixon Ticonderoga Co said on Tuesday it repurchased 9.9 million shares, or 30 percent, of it publicly-held subsidiary Dixon Ticonderoga de Mexico SA de CV for about $2.5 million.
The purchase increased Dixon's ownership in the subsidiary to about 80.1 percent from 50.1 percent, the company said.

Dixon Mexico makes and markets wood-case graphite and coloring pencils, crayons, felt-tip markers and other similar products, while U.S.-based Dixon Ticonderoga makes and markets writing instruments, light-art and office supplies.

"We are extremely pleased to have increased our ownership in a very profitable and growing company at a nearly 40 percent discount form the price at which we sold the shares in the initial public offering more than two years ago," Dixon Ticonderoga President Gino Pala said.
The company said it paid about $0.25 for each Dixon Mexico share.
